features.name: age_bucket
features.description: Ordinal age bucket capturing life stage: 0=<25, 1=25-34, 2=35-44, 3=45-54, 4=55-64, 5=65+.
features.expected_model_benefit: Trees can split on coarse life-stage groups that correlate with earning potential.

features.name: hours_bucket
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures nonlinear effect of work intensity that tree splits exploit cleanly.

features.name: has_capital_gain
features.description: Boolean indicator that the row reports any capital gain.
features.expected_model_benefit: Capital gain is highly skewed with most zeros; a binary flag gives a clean split.

features.name: has_capital_loss
features.description: Boolean indicator that the row reports any capital loss.
features.expected_model_benefit: Sparse but informative; a flag gives trees a clean split on nonzero loss.

features.name: net_capital_flow
features.description: Net capital activity: capital_gain minus capital_loss, on log1p-signed scale for tail compression.
features.expected_model_benefit: Combines two sparse columns into one signed magnitude useful for threshold splits.

features.name: high_capital_gain_flag
features.description: Indicator that capital_gain exceeds a high threshold (>=5000), a known strong wealth signal.
features.expected_model_benefit: Sharp threshold above which earnings prior shifts strongly; tree-friendly.

features.name: education_level_group
features.description: Coarse education ordinal grouping based on education_num: 0=<HS, 1=HS-grad, 2=some-college/assoc, 3=bachelors, 4=advanced.
features.expected_model_benefit: Aggregates fine-grained education codes into stable ordinal tiers for cleaner splits.

features.name: age_education_interaction
features.description: Product of age and education_num capturing combined experience-and-credentials effect.
features.expected_model_benefit: Interactions between age and education are nonlinear; an explicit product helps shallow trees.

features.name: hours_x_education
features.description: Interaction of working hours and education_num: proxy for skilled labor intensity.
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures that high education plus long hours combine multiplicatively for earnings.

features.name: is_prime_working_age
features.description: Boolean flag for prime earning years (age between 30 and 55 inclusive).
features.expected_model_benefit: Encodes a known peak-earning window for a single clean tree split.

features.name: demographic_stability_score
features.description: Semantic ordinal judgment of likely household/economic stability combining marital_status, relationship, and age. Higher = more stable established household. 0=very young/unattached, 1=young single, 2=mid single or separated, 3=established couple/family, 4=long-term partnered with mature age.
features.expected_model_benefit: Tree models gain a compact ordinal that summarizes interacting demographic signals without needing deep splits across multiple columns.

features.name: occupation_skill_tier
features.description: Semantic tier of occupation skill/compensation potential based on the occupation code interpretation. 0=low-skill manual/service, 1=semi-skilled trades/clerical, 2=skilled technical/sales, 3=professional/managerial/specialty. Assigned from row's occupation and workclass codes.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a domain-informed ordinal grouping over occupation categories that gives trees a strong single-feature split for earning potential.
